summary: Repaired node1’s upload endpoint. It atomically stores unique receipts up to 65,536 bytes, rejects larger bodies with HTTP 413, returns 404 for other paths, survives interrupted requests and reboots, and preserves the legacy receipt.
actions_performed: Replaced the unsafe legacy Python handler with bounded, atomic receipt handling.
Created a dedicated non-login service account and hardened, enabled systemd service.
Restricted TCP 8080 through firewalld to node2.
Preserved the original server as a root-only rollback copy.
Verified exact-limit, oversized, separate-file, interrupted-request, and routing behavior from node2.
Sequentially rebooted node1 and node2 and verified changed boot identities and recovery.
Left five accepted validation uploads as required receipts; no partial files remain.

evidence.requirement: Accept raw bodies through 65,536 bytes with identical stored bytes.
evidence.summary: The 65,536-byte request returned HTTP 200; source and receipt SHA-256 both equal 7daca2095d0438260fa849183dfc67faa459fdf4936e1bc91eec6b281b27e4c2.
Distinct accepted requests produced uniquely named mode-0600 receipts with matching hashes. Final completed receipt count is five.

evidence.requirement: Reject bodies larger than 65,536 bytes with HTTP 413 before publication.
evidence.summary: A 65,537-byte request returned 413 without increasing the receipt count; an Expect request was rejected before any body bytes were transmitted.

evidence.requirement: Interrupted requests leave no completed receipt.
evidence.summary: Closing after 140 of 10,000 declared bytes left the completed count unchanged and temporary_count=0.
Both POST and GET requests to unrelated paths returned 404, including after both reboots.
received/prior.bin remains 28 bytes, root-owned, with unchanged SHA-256 ac9690aa0a0fe733a2702464777a0148b5a189d0a2f6eef1993268ebc70665fe.
The endpoint runs under the dedicated http-upload account; its hardened service is enabled and active, TCP 8080 is listening, the node2-scoped firewall rule persists, and no units are failed.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel.

evidence.summary: Boot ID changed from f455a75c-ec12-49a8-a647-c2be3f67c08c to 4d79f27f-a84b-49b2-9054-976e702e5eb6. Service, firewall, receipts, and live 200/413/404 behavior recovered.
Boot ID changed from b953e8ce-b303-4022-826c-3b5910ad1e9b to 35ac0ca3-8a3e-429c-b37a-90e5e7e80e41. Its IP, route, and application-client behavior recovered.
